mainTopic: The husband's duty to give his wife shoes and clothing (כתובות סה:): why three pairs of shoes but only one set of clothes, the value of 'fifty זוז', and who keeps worn-out clothes
overview: This amud finishes the chapter אף על פי and begins the chapter מציאת האשה. First the גמרא explains the משנה's rules about the wife's support. She gets three pairs of shoes a year because the משנה is talking about mountain country, and they are given on יום טוב. 'Fifty זוז' for clothing means cheap local coins. Her worn-out clothes are hers to wear during נדה, but a widow's worn clothes go to the heirs. רב נחמן and רב אשי argue whether 'she eats with him' on Friday night means real eating or תשמיש, and both challenges to רב אשי are answered. רבי עולא רבה teaches that a father must feed his very young children until age six. The attempted proof from a nursing wife's extra food is pushed off, and רבי יהושע בן לוי adds that she gets wine. The new chapter's משנה sorts a wife's finds, earnings, inheritance and injury payments between her and her husband. The גמרא explains that the new point is the dispute over בושת and פגם. Then a ברייתא about a wife's finds is recited before רבא, who begins a challenge that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Naked but wearing shoes
steps.stepSummary: A challenge: the משנה's תנא gives the wife shoes three times a year but clothing only once, which seems backwards.
steps.simpleTranslation: This תנא leaves her naked but wearing shoes!
steps.whatsHappening: Someone attacks the משנה's list. She gets new shoes at each of the three festivals but new clothes only once a year, so it sounds like her clothes are worn out while her shoes are new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge is about proportion. Clothing is more basic than shoes, so why would shoes be given more often? The picture of a woman 'naked with shoes' shows how strange the ruling looks.

keyTerms.meaning: The teacher of the משנה, the author of this ruling

phrases.english: This tanna
leaves her stripped naked but wearing shoes!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי תַּנָּא שְׁלִיחַ עַרְטִלַאי וּרְמֵי מְסָאנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the משנה's rule about shoes given three times a year versus clothes once a year.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ratio of three pairs of shoes to one set of clothes per year
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Clothing is more essential than shoes, so giving shoes more often than clothes makes no sense.

steps.title: The משנה is talking about mountain country
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the משנה is describing a hilly area, where shoes wear out quickly and three pairs a year are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The תנא is speaking about a mountainous place, where she cannot manage without three pairs of shoes.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends the משנה by explaining the setting. In the mountains shoes wear out fast, so she really does need three pairs a year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The number of shoes is not about how important shoes are compared to clothes. It is about how fast each one wears out. Rough mountain ground ruins shoes long before clothes are worn out, so the ratio is fair.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not possible to manage

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: תַּנָּא בִּמְקוֹם הָרִים קָאֵי,
phrases.english: He said to him: The tanna is standing in a mountainous region,
phrases.notes: 'Standing in' means the תנא is talking about that kind of place.

phrases.aramaic: דְּלָא סַגִּיא בְּלָא תְּלָתָא זוּגֵי מְסָאנֵי.
phrases.english: where she cannot manage without three pairs of shoes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: תַּנָּא בִּמְקוֹם הָרִים קָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case to a specific setting (mountainous terrain)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה looked like it gave shoes more weight than clothing for no reason.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is describing a place where shoes wear out quickly, so three pairs a year is simply what she needs.

steps.title: Give the shoes on a יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: Along the way, the משנה also teaches that the shoes should be given on the festivals so she can enjoy them on the יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in passing it teaches us that he should give them to her on the festival, so that she will have joy through them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a side lesson from the משנה's wording: it times the shoes 'from festival to festival' because they should be handed over on the יום טוב itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once we know three pairs are needed, the משנה could have said any three times a year. It chose the festivals to teach that new shoes add to her שמחת יום טוב.

phrases.english: And in passing it teaches us
that he should give them to her on the festival,
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the shoes, which the משנה gives from one festival to the next.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֵיכִי דְּנֶיהְוֵי לַהּ שִׂמְחָה בְּגַוַּיְיהוּ.
phrases.english: so that she will have joy through them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further lesson on top of אביי's answer in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The shoes should be given on the festivals so they add to her festival joy.
steps.whatToRemember: Three pairs of shoes a year fits a mountain region where shoes wear out fast, and they are given on the festivals to add to her שמחה.

steps.title: Fifty זוז means cheap local coins
steps.stepSummary: On the משנה's 'clothes worth fifty זוז', אביי says this means fifty 'simple' (low-value) זוז.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And clothes worth fifty זוז.' אביי said: Fifty simple זוז.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, and אביי explains that the 'fifty זוז' are a cheap local coin, not full-value זוז.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The amount stays the same, but אביי changes what kind of coin is meant. That makes the real value of the clothing much smaller.

keyTerms.meaning: A silver coin, the same as a דינר
Simple or plain coins, worth much less than standard ones

phrases.english: And clothes worth fifty zuz.
Abaye said: Fifty simple zuz.
phrases.notes: 'Simple' coins were the cheap local money, worth only a small part of a full זוז.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵלִים שֶׁל חֲמִשִּׁים זוּז. אָמַר אַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's fifty זוז refers to low-value 'simple' coins.

steps.title: How do we know?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for אביי's source.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what proves אביי's reading. This line sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain words of the משנה just say 'fifty זוז.' So אביי needs to show something in the משנה that forces the cheaper meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? How do we know?

phrases.english: From where?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What in the משנה shows that fifty זוז means cheap coins?

steps.title: A poor man could not afford real זוז
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says these amounts are for the poorest Jews. A pauper could never pay fifty full זוז, so the coins must be cheap ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it teaches: When is this said? For the poorest in Israel, but for a respected man everything goes according to his status. And if you think it means actually fifty זוז, where would a poor man get fifty זוז?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the משנה's own statement that these amounts are for a very poor man. Then it argues that real fifty זוז would be far too much for such a man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה sets the minimum for the poorest husband. Fifty full זוז is a large sum that a pauper does not have. So the amount only fits if it is measured in cheap coins.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case are these words said?
And if it enters your mind (that…)

phrases.english: From that it teaches: In what case are these things said?
— regarding the poorest in Israel,
but for a respected man — everything is according to his status.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ חֲמִשִּׁים זוּז מַמָּשׁ,
phrases.english: And if it enters your mind that it means literally fifty zuz,
a poor man, where would he get fifty zuz?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5 with a proof.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that fifty זוז means cheap coins
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's statement that these amounts apply to the poorest Jews

steps.title: Proven: cheap coins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the משנה means fifty simple זוז.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this: fifty simple זוז.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the proof and confirms אביי's reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full-value reading does not work for a poor man, so the only reading left is the cheap-coin one.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this, so it is proven

phrases.english: Rather, learn from this:
fifty simple zuz.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the proof in step 6.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה's fifty זוז of clothing means fifty low-value coins, an amount a poor husband can manage.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's amounts are the minimum for the poorest husband, so 'fifty זוז' must mean cheap coins. A richer man gives according to his status.

steps.title: Leftover food goes to him, worn clothes to her
steps.stepSummary: On the משנה's line about new and worn clothing, a ברייתא teaches: leftover food belongs to the husband, and leftover worn clothes belong to the wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And they do not give her new ones…' The רבנן taught: Leftover food belongs to the husband; leftover worn clothes belong to the wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and brings a ברייתא about who keeps what is left over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food and clothing are treated differently. Extra food the wife did not eat goes back to the husband, but old clothes she has replaced stay with her.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין נוֹתְנִין לָהּ לֹא חֲדָשִׁים וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: And they do not give her new ones, etc.
The Rabbis taught: Leftover food belongs to the husband,
leftover worn clothes belong to the wife.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין נוֹתְנִין לָהּ לֹא חֲדָשִׁים וְכוּ׳. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Leftover food goes to the husband; leftover worn clothes go to the wife.

steps.title: Why does she need old clothes?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what use the wife has for worn-out clothes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Leftover worn clothes go to the wife — why does she need them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the second half of the ברייתא. She already has new clothes, so why give her the old ones? This sets up רחבה's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the husband gets leftover food, we might expect him to get the old clothes too. So the גמרא wants a reason why the clothes go to her.

phrases.english: Leftover worn clothes to the wife — why does she need them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reason behind the ברייתא in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What purpose do worn clothes serve for a wife who already has new ones?

steps.title: She wears them during נדה
steps.stepSummary: רחבה explains that she wears the old clothes during her נדה days so she does not become unattractive to her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: רחבה said: She covers herself with them during her days of נדה, so that she will not become repulsive to her husband.
steps.whatsHappening: רחבה gives the reason. The worn clothes are for her נדה days, so her good clothes stay pleasant for when she is with her husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule protects the closeness of the marriage. If she wore her nice clothes during נדה, they might later become unpleasant to him. Keeping separate old clothes for those days prevents that.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַחֲבָה: שֶׁמִּתְכַּסָּה בָּהֶן בִּימֵי נִדָּתָהּ,
phrases.english: Rahava said: Because she covers herself with them during her days of menstruation,
so that she will not become repulsive to her husband.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַחֲבָה: שֶׁמִּתְכַּסָּה בָּהֶן בִּימֵי נִדָּתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She needs the worn clothes to wear during נדה, so she stays attractive to her husband.

steps.title: A widow's worn clothes go to the heirs
steps.stepSummary: אביי reports a tradition: the worn clothes of a widow belong to her late husband's heirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: We hold that a widow's leftover worn clothes go to his heirs.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds a new ruling. Once the husband has died, the old clothes do not stay with the widow. They go to his heirs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is an exception to the ברייתא's rule that worn clothes belong to the wife. It applies only after the husband's death.

keyTerms.meaning: We hold, we have a tradition

phrases.english: Abaye said: We hold,
the leftover worn clothes of a widow belong to his heirs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the ברייתא's rule to the case of a widow and reaches a different result.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A widow's worn clothes belong to the husband's heirs.

steps.title: The reason no longer applies
steps.stepSummary: The reason the wife keeps old clothes is so she stays attractive to her husband. With the husband gone, that reason disappears.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the point is that she not become repulsive in his eyes; here, let her become repulsive.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains אביי's ruling using רחבה's reason. That reason only matters while the husband is alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wife's right to the worn clothes comes from protecting the marriage. The heirs do not need her to look attractive to them, so the clothes go back to the husband's estate.

keyTerms.meaning: In his face, in his eyes

phrases.english: There it is so that she not become repulsive in his eyes;
phrases.notes: 'There' means the ברייתא's case of a living husband, using רחבה's reason.

phrases.english: here — let her become repulsive, and so be it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind אביי's ruling in step 11.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Because the wife keeps worn clothes only to stay attractive to her husband, a widow's worn clothes go to the heirs.
steps.whatToRemember: Leftover food goes to the husband and worn clothes go to the wife, so she can wear them during נדה and stay attractive to him. Once he dies that reason is gone, so a widow's worn clothes go to the heirs.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how the reason behind a rule decides how far the rule reaches. When the reason does not apply, the rule changes.

steps.title: What does "she eats" mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about the silver מעה and asks what the word "אוכלת" (she eats) means there.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: "He gives her a silver מעה, etc." (and she eats with him on Friday night). What does "she eats" mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה and asking what one word means. It is setting up a disagreement that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the wife "eats with him" on Friday nights. The word could be taken literally or as a polite hint at something else. The גמרא wants to know which one is meant.

keyTerms.meaning: A silver מעה, a small coin the husband gives his wife for small weekly needs
"She eats", the word the גמרא is asking about

phrases.english: "He gives her a silver ma'ah, etc."
What does "she eats" mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the clothing discussion to the next line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether "אוכלת" in the משנה means real eating or something else.

steps.title: Real eating or marital relations
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says it means real eating. רב אשי says it refers to תשמיש (marital relations).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: she really eats with him. רב אשי said: it means marital relations.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give two different answers to the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב נחמן, the husband must have his wife dine with him once a week, on Friday night. For רב אשי, the word "eats" is a hint, and the משנה is really saying he must be with his wife on Friday night.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: she literally eats.
Rav Ashi said: it means marital relations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13 with two opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב נחמן: real eating. רב אשי: תשמיש.

steps.title: Why would the משנה say "eats"?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב אשי: if the משנה means relations, why does it use the word "eats"?
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: she eats with him on Friday nights. For the one who says it means eating, that is why it says "she eats". But for the one who says it means relations, why say "she eats"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב אשי's reading using the plain wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "אוכלת" fits רב נחמן perfectly. For רב אשי it seems like the wrong word, since the משנה could have just said what it meant.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense for one view (but not for the other)
According to the one who says

phrases.english: We learned: she eats with him on Friday nights.
It makes sense according to the one who says it means eating,
that is why it says "she eats".
But according to the one who says it means relations,
why does it say "she eats"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אשי's opinion from step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי, who reads "אוכלת" as תשמיש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's word "eats" fits only the literal reading, so why use it if relations is meant?

steps.title: A polite way of speaking
steps.stepSummary: The משנה uses a clean way of speaking, and a פסוק in משלי also uses "eating" to hint at relations.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a clean, polite way of speaking, as the פסוק says: "She eats and wipes her mouth and says: I have done nothing wrong."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב אשי: the משנה chose a polite word on purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה avoids speaking openly about private matters, so it says "eats". The proof is a פסוק in משלי that describes a sinning woman as one who "eats and wipes her mouth", where eating clearly hints at relations.

keyTerms.meaning: A clean, refined way of speaking
As it is written (in a פסוק)

phrases.english: It is a refined way of speaking,
as it is written: "She eats and wipes her mouth
and says: I have done no wrong."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the wording as a deliberate polite expression
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word "eats" must mean real eating.
steps.terutzMaskana: "Eats" can be a refined hint at relations, as in משלי.

steps.title: Challenge from רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: what about שבת day?
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says she eats with him Friday night and on שבת. For רב אשי this would mean relations by day, but רב הונא said Jews do not do that by day.
steps.simpleTranslation: We have a challenge: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says she eats on Friday night and on שבת. For the one who says it means eating, that is why it says "and שבת". But for the one who says it means relations, are there relations on שבת day? רב הונא said: the Jewish people are holy and do not have relations during the day!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second, stronger challenge to רב אשי from a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Adding "and שבת" means daytime too. Eating by day is no problem, but relations by day goes against רב הונא's rule, so רב אשי's reading seems impossible here.

phrases.aramaic: מֵיתִיבִי, רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: They challenged: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
She eats on Friday nights and on Shabbat.
It makes sense according to the one who says it means eating,
that is why it says "and Shabbat".
But according to the one who says it means relations,
are there relations on Shabbat day?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַב הוּנָא: יִשְׂרָאֵל קְדוֹשִׁים הֵן,
phrases.english: But Rav Huna said: the Jewish people are holy,
and they do not have relations during the day!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי, רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge to רב אשי after the first one was answered.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's reading of "אוכלת" as תשמיש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל includes Shabbat day, and relations by day goes against רב הונא's rule.

steps.title: In a dark house it is allowed
steps.stepSummary: רבא said that in a dark house, relations by day are allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבא said: in a dark house it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with a statement of רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's rule is about daylight. If the room is dark, the problem goes away, so רבן שמעון בן גמליאל can still mean relations on שבת day, and רב אשי stands.
steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן reads "אוכלת" as real eating, and רב אשי reads it as תשמיש. Both challenges to רב אשי are answered: the word is a polite hint, and daytime is fine in a dark house.

phrases.english: Rava already said: in a dark house it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits רב הונא's rule with an exception
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Relations by day are never done, so Shabbat day cannot mean relations.
steps.terutzMaskana: In a dark house it is permitted, so רב אשי's reading works.

steps.title: A father must feed his very young children
steps.stepSummary: On the משנה's line about a nursing mother, רבי עולא רבה teaches publicly that although a father is not obligated to feed his young children, he must feed the very young ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: "And if she was nursing." רבי עולא רבה taught at the entrance of the house of the נשיא: Even though they said that a person does not have to feed his young sons and daughters, he does have to feed the very young ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line in the משנה about a nursing mother and brings a teaching about feeding small children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known rule that a father is not obligated to feed his young children. רבי עולא רבה adds a limit: the very youngest children he must feed. This connects to the nursing mother, whose baby is among the very young.

keyTerms.meaning: The house of the נשיא, the leader of the Jewish people

phrases.english: "And if she was nursing."
Rabbi Ulla the Great taught publicly
at the entrance of the house of the Nasi:
Even though they said

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אָדָם זָן אֶת בָּנָיו וּבְנוֹתָיו כְּשֶׁהֵן קְטַנִּים,
phrases.english: that a person does not have to feed his sons and daughters when they are young,
he does feed the very young ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרֵשׁ רַבִּי עוּלָּא רַבָּה אַפִּיתְחָא דְּבֵי נְשִׂיאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic on the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A father is not obligated to feed his young children, but he must feed the very young ones.

steps.title: Until what age?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how long a child counts as 'very young' for רבי עולא רבה's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Until what age?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question about the rule just taught. It is setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עולא רבה said a father must feed his very young children. Now we need to know where 'very young' ends.

keyTerms.meaning: Until how much / until what point?

phrases.english: Until when?
phrases.notes: He's asking: until what age is a child still one of the 'very young' ones his father must feed?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the age limit of the rule taught in step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The age at which a child stops counting as 'very young'.

steps.title: Until age six, like רב אסי
steps.stepSummary: A child counts as very young until six, matching רב אסי's rule that a six-year-old goes with his mother's עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Until age six, like רב אסי. רב אסי said: a six-year-old child can go out using his mother's עירוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: until age six. It backs this up with a rule of רב אסי about עירוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אסי treats a six-year-old as still attached to his mother, so he walks on שבת by her עירוב. The same age is used here: up to six, a child is still 'very young' and his father must feed him.

keyTerms.meaning: Like the view of רב אסי
The Shabbat arrangement that lets a person walk beyond the normal limit

phrases.english: Until six years old, like רב אסי.
For רב אסי said:

phrases.aramaic: קָטָן בֶּן שֵׁשׁ יוֹצֵא בְּעֵירוּב אִמּוֹ.
phrases.english: A six-year-old child goes out with his mother's עירוב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Until age six, based on רב אסי's עירוב rule.

steps.title: Where does this rule come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of רבי עולא רבה's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source for the rule that a father must feed his very young children. It is setting up an attempted proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now we only had רבי עולא רבה's statement. Now the גמרא wants to find it hinted in the משנה itself.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? What is the source?

phrases.english: From where?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the age limit to the source of the rule itself.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source for the father's duty to feed very young children.

steps.title: Proof from the nursing wife's extra food
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives a nursing wife more food and less work. This seems to be because the baby eats with her, so the father is feeding his baby.
steps.simpleTranslation: From what the משנה teaches: if she was nursing, they lower her work quota and add to her food. Why? Isn't it because the baby needs to eat along with her?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to prove the rule from our משנה. The extra food for a nursing wife must be for the baby.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the husband gives more food because the baby feeds from her, then he is really paying for his baby's food. That would show a father must support his very young child.

keyTerms.meaning: Her handiwork, the work quota she owes her husband

phrases.english: From what it teaches: if she was nursing,
they reduce her work quota,
and they add to her food.
What is the reason?
Is it not because he needs to eat along with her?
phrases.notes: 'He' is the baby. Since the baby drinks her milk, it is as if he eats her food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 22 with a proof from the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: The father's duty to feed his very young child.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's rule that a nursing wife gets more food and less work.

steps.title: Maybe it is because she is sick
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed off: maybe she gets more food because nursing makes her weak, not because of the baby.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe it is because she is sick.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof. The extra food may be for the wife herself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a nursing woman counts as sick, her husband feeds her more because of his duty to his wife. Then the משנה says nothing about a duty to the child.

phrases.english: But perhaps it is because she is sick.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes off the proof in step 23.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the nursing-wife rule.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The extra food can be explained by the wife's own weakness, without any duty to the child.

steps.title: Then why not just say 'sick'?
steps.stepSummary: If sickness were the reason, the משנה should have said 'if she was sick.' It said 'nursing,' so the baby must be the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let it teach 'if she was sick.' Why does it say 'if she was nursing'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the rejection by looking at the משנה's exact words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה chose the word 'nursing,' not 'sick.' That choice seems to point to the baby as the reason, which would bring back the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it teach, it should have said

phrases.english: If so, let it teach: 'If she was sick.'
Why does it say 'if she was nursing'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rejection in step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the extra food is only because she is sick.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If sickness were the reason, the משנה would have said 'sick' instead of 'nursing.'

steps.title: Nursing women usually count as sick
steps.stepSummary: The משנה said 'nursing' to teach that nursing women are normally treated as sick, so the proof still fails.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps this is what it teaches us: nursing women are normally considered sick.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the rejection. The word 'nursing' itself teaches something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is telling us that every nursing woman counts as sick, even without real illness. So the extra food can still be for her, and the proof for the child's support falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches us

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean a father has no duty to feed his young children. רבי עולא רבה's rule still stands; only this proof from the משנה is lost.

phrases.english: But perhaps it teaches us this:
that ordinary nursing women are sick.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 25 and keeps the rejection of the proof.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a new purpose to the משנה's choice of words.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word 'nursing' must point to the baby.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word teaches that nursing women normally count as sick, so the proof is not conclusive.

steps.title: A nursing wife also gets wine
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי says a nursing wife is given extra wine, because wine is good for milk.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was said: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: they add wine for her, because wine is good for milk.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more rule about the nursing wife: besides extra food, she gets wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds to the משנה's list of what a nursing wife receives. The reason given is practical: wine helps her make milk.
steps.whatToRemember: A nursing wife gets less work, more food, and wine. A father must feed his very young children until six, but the משנה about nursing is not a clear proof for that.

phrases.aramaic: אִיתְּמַר, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
phrases.english: It was stated: רבי יהושע בן לוי said:
They add wine for her,
because wine is good for milk.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the nursing-wife rule and adds a detail.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A nursing wife is given extra wine, since wine helps milk.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter אף על פי
steps.stepSummary: The chapter אף על פי ends.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter 'אף על פי'.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the closing line of the chapter, saying we hope to come back and learn it again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No new law is taught here. It marks the end of the chapter.

phrases.english: We will return to you, 'Even though'.
phrases.notes: 'אף על פי' is the chapter's name, taken from the first words of its first משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the last teaching.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: End of chapter אף על פי.

steps.title: New chapter: what the husband gets and what the wife keeps
steps.stepSummary: The משנה opens the chapter מציאת האשה. The wife's finds and earnings go to her husband. He eats the profits of her inheritance while she is alive. The payments for her shame and damage are hers.
steps.simpleTranslation: What a wife finds and what she earns belong to her husband. Her inheritance stays hers, but he gets its profits while she is alive. Money paid for her shame and her damage belongs to her.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter starts with a משנה that sorts the wife's money into what goes to the husband and what stays with her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three levels here. The husband fully gets her finds and earnings. With her inheritance, the property stays hers but he gets the income. The payments for בושת and פגם stay entirely hers.

keyTerms.meaning: A lost object that someone finds
Her earnings, what she makes with her work
Gets the income or profits of property without owning the property itself
Payment for shame or humiliation caused by an attacker
Payment for the loss in her value caused by an injury

steps.whatToRemember: Finds and earnings go to the husband. He gets the profits of her inheritance. Payments for shame and damage are hers.

phrases.english: A lost object found by the wife
and her earnings belong to her husband.
And her inheritance: he eats the profits during her lifetime.
Her shame payment and her damage payment are hers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new chapter after the chapter אף על פי ended in step 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wife's finds and earnings go to her husband. He eats the profits of her inheritance. Payments for her בושת and פגם belong to her.

steps.title: A different view: split the injury payments by where the injury is
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בן בתירא splits the shame and damage payments. For a hidden injury, she gets two-thirds and he gets one-third. For a visible injury, he gets two-thirds and she gets one-third. His share is paid right away. Land is bought with her share, and he eats its profits.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה בן בתירא says: if the injury is in a hidden place, she gets two parts and he gets one. If it is in a visible place, he gets two parts and she gets one. His share is given to him right away. Her share is used to buy land, and he gets the profits.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings רבי יהודה בן בתירא, who disagrees with the first opinion about the payments for shame and damage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion gave these payments entirely to the wife. רבי יהודה בן בתירא holds that the husband is also hurt by her injury, so he gets a share. The bigger share goes to whoever is hurt more. Even her share is turned into land so that he can get its profits.

keyTerms.meaning: In a hidden place on the body
In a visible place on the body

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira says:
When the injury is in a hidden place,
she gets two parts, and he gets one.
And when it is in a visible place,
he gets two parts, and she gets one.
His share is given right away,
and with her share, land is bought,
and he eats the profits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first opinion's ruling that the payments for בושת and פגם belong entirely to the wife.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The payments for shame and damage are split two-to-one. The person hurt more by the injury, depending on whether it is hidden or visible, gets the larger share. Land is bought with the wife's share, and the husband eats its profits.

steps.title: Why repeat this? An earlier משנה already taught it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the משנה adds. An earlier משנה taught that a father gets his daughter's finds and earnings, and that a husband gets everything a father gets plus the profits of her property.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the משנה teaching us? We already learned that a father has rights over his daughter: her קידושין (by money, document, or relations), her finds, her earnings, and canceling her vows. He receives her גט, but he does not eat the profits of her property. Once she marries, the husband has more than the father, because he does eat the profits.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges our משנה by asking what it adds. An older משנה already seems to cover the same rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier משנה says the husband has everything the father has, plus more. The father gets her finds and earnings, so the husband surely does too. The "plus more" is the profits of her property. So the first part of our משנה looks like a repeat.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it teaching us? (asked when a teaching seems to add nothing new)
Is entitled to, has the rights to

steps.confusionAlert: The quoted list is about a father and his daughter, not about a husband. The point is the last line, which says the husband gets all of that plus more.

phrases.english: Gemara: What is it teaching us?
We already learned:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה from earlier in this מסכת, about a daughter who is still under her father.

phrases.english: The father is entitled to his daughter's betrothal,
whether by money, by document, or by relations.
He is entitled to her finds and her earnings
and to canceling her vows.
He receives her bill of divorce,
but he does not eat the profits during her lifetime.
Once she marries, the husband has more than him,
since he eats the profits during her lifetime.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why the משנה in step 29 needed to state rules that seem to be already known.
steps.kashyaTarget: The first part of our משנה, which says finds and earnings go to the husband and he eats the profits of her inheritance.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The earlier משנה already shows that the husband gets everything a father gets (finds and earnings) plus the profits of her property. So our משנה seems to add nothing new.

steps.title: The new part is shame and damage, which are disputed
steps.stepSummary: The משנה needed to teach about the payments for shame and damage. This is the new information, because רבי יהודה בן בתירא and the רבנן argue about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It needed to teach about her shame and damage payments, which are the subject of a מחלוקת between רבי יהודה בן בתירא and the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The real reason for the משנה is the rule about shame and damage payments, which was never taught before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא agrees that the finds, earnings, and profits were already known. They are repeated only as a lead-in. The new teaching is who owns the בושת and פגם payments, and on that the רבנן and רבי יהודה בן בתירא disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: He needed it, meaning this was the necessary part to teach
The Rabbis, here the first opinion in the משנה

steps.whatToRemember: Our משנה is needed for the new rule about shame and damage payments. The other rules were already known from the earlier משנה.

phrases.english: Her shame and her damage, that is what it needed to teach,

phrases.aramaic: פְּלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתֵירָא וְרַבָּנַן.
phrases.english: the dispute between Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira and the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: "The Rabbis" are the first, unnamed opinion in our משנה, who said these payments belong to her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 31 by pointing to the new part of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies the new teaching: the משנה is needed for a rule not taught before.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole משנה seemed to repeat the earlier משנה about father and husband.
steps.terutzMaskana: The new teaching is the ownership of the בושת and פגם payments, which is a מחלוקת between רבי יהודה בן בתירא and the רבנן. The rest is a lead-in.

steps.title: A ברייתא: the wife keeps her own finds
steps.stepSummary: A תנא recites a ברייתא before רבא. The first opinion says a wife's find belongs to her. רבי עקיבא says it belongs to her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: A reciter taught in front of רבא: Something a wife finds belongs to her. רבי עקיבא says: it belongs to her husband.
steps.whatsHappening: A new source is brought: a ברייתא about who owns what a wife finds. The first view says she keeps it, and רבי עקיבא says the husband gets it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה said plainly that the wife's finds go to the husband. This ברייתא gives that ruling only to רבי עקיבא, while the first opinion lets the wife keep her finds. In the next step רבא challenges how the ברייתא assigns these opinions, using a קל וחומר from her extra earnings.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, a person whose job was to memorize and recite ברייתות in the בית מדרש
A lost object that someone finds

steps.confusionAlert: Here the word תַּנָּא does not mean a sage of the משנה. It means a reciter who repeated ברייתות out loud before the אמוראים.

phrases.english: A reciter taught in front of Rava:
The find of a wife belongs to herself.
Rabbi Akiva says: to her husband.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא on the wife's finds. Its first opinion differs from the משנה in step 29.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first opinion: a wife's find is hers. רבי עקיבא: it is her husband's.

steps.title: רבא begins a challenge from the wife's extra earnings
steps.stepSummary: רבא responds to the reciter. He opens a 'how much more so' argument based on העדפה, the wife's extra earnings.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Now, if the extra earnings...
steps.whatsHappening: רבא starts to push back against the ברייתא. This line only sets up his argument, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words הַשְׁתָּא וּמָה signal a קל וחומר: 'if this is true about X, then surely it is true about Y.' רבא plans to compare a wife's find to her העדפה, the earnings beyond the amount the חכמים set. He will use that comparison to show the ברייתא as recited does not fit.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Now, if...'; the opening of a 'how much more so' argument
Surplus; what a wife earns beyond the set minimum amount of work

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: רבא is speaking to the reciter who just said the ברייתא.

phrases.english: Now, if the surplus earnings,
phrases.notes: The sentence isn't finished yet. רבא completes his point on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts an attack on the ברייתא just recited.
steps.kashyaTarget: How the ברייתא recited in step 33 assigns the opinions
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר from העדפה to מציאה (the full argument continues past this point)
